text: I understand DBN's strategic priorities clearly enough to explain them in my own words.
I understand how my role contributes to DBN's mandate and strategic objectives.
When priorities compete, I know what DBN's strategy says should come first.
In my area, day-to-day decisions and work priorities are guided by DBN's strategic direction.
Work between departments is coordinated around shared DBN outcomes, not only departmental priorities.
DBN's systems and processes make it easy for teams to share information and complete work across functions.
When work moves from one team to another, responsibilities, timelines and handovers are clear.
Leaders and managers make decisions with the impact on the full DBN value chain in mind.
My role, responsibilities, performance expectations and decision boundaries are clear.
Performance standards in my area are clear, measurable and applied consistently.
Decisions and agreed actions are followed through within reasonable timeframes.
Underperformance or non-delivery is addressed fairly, directly and timeously.
I understand DBN's purpose and why its work matters for Namibia.
I can see a clear link between my work and DBN's development mandate.
DBN's purpose gives meaning to the work I do.
I am proud of the impact DBN is working to create.
I understand where decisions that affect my work should be made and who has authority to make them.
Decisions are made at the right level without unnecessary escalation.
Decisions that affect my work are communicated clearly and in time for me to act on them.
Approval processes help manage risk without unnecessarily delaying delivery.
My contribution to DBN's work is noticed and acknowledged in a fair way.
Recognition, reward and progression are based on contribution and performance, not personal relationships.
I receive regular, honest feedback that helps me understand how I am performing.
Good performance is recognised in ways that encourage accountability, motivation and growth.
Leaders seek to understand issues properly before drawing conclusions.
Feedback from employees is treated as useful information, even when it is difficult to hear.
Lessons from work, projects and setbacks are shared so that teams can improve.
Employee feedback and lessons learned lead to visible improvements in how work is done at DBN.
My manager gives clear and consistent direction about priorities and expectations.
My manager is accessible when I need guidance, clarity or support.
My manager models the standards and behaviours they expect from others.
My manager helps create a team environment where people can perform, learn and work well together.
I can raise concerns about work issues without fear of negative consequences.
People can respectfully question ideas or decisions, regardless of level or position.
Mistakes are discussed in a way that supports learning and improvement, not blame.
I feel respected and valued at DBN as a person, not only for the work I deliver.
I am encouraged to suggest better ways of working, even when they challenge existing practice.
When a well-considered new approach does not work, it is treated as a learning opportunity.
DBN creates space for people across teams to develop and test new ideas.
New ideas that can improve DBN's mandate delivery are supported with enough time, attention or resources to move forward.
My team adapts effectively when priorities, conditions or stakeholder demands change.
Under pressure, we find practical solutions without compromising quality, ethics or service.
Decisions are made quickly enough to keep important work moving.
After setbacks or disruptions, DBN reflects, learns and adjusts its approach.
I understand who depends on my work, both inside and outside DBN, and what they need from me.
We consider the impact of our decisions on customers, stakeholders and internal service users.
Customer and stakeholder needs shape how DBN plans, prioritises and improves work.
When a customer or stakeholder raises a concern, it is taken seriously and responded to within a reasonable time.
